Yesterday my brother eat breakfast late.
Yesterday my brother ate breakfast late.
Use ate for a completed action yesterday.
They was waiting outside.
They were waiting outside.
Use were with they.
My sister have two bicycles.
My sister has two bicycles.
Use has with one person, such as my sister.
We has enough time.
We have enough time.
Use have with we.
He didn't wrote the email.
He didn't write the email.
After didn't, use the base form write.
Can you helps me?
Can you help me?
After can, use the base form help.
I am agree with you.
I agree with you.
Agree is a verb here; it does not need am.
She is more taller than me.
She is taller than me.
Taller already expresses the comparison; remove more.
There are a problem.
There is a problem.
Use is with the singular a problem.
There is three chairs.
There are three chairs.
Use are with plural chairs.
He gave me an useful tip.
He gave me a useful tip.
Useful starts with a consonant sound, so use a.
We waited for a hour.
We waited for an hour.
Hour starts with a vowel sound, so use an.
I have lived here since five years.
I have lived here for five years.
Use for with a duration such as five years.
She enjoys to swim.
She enjoys swimming.
After enjoys, use the -ing form.
I look forward to meet you.
I look forward to meeting you.
The to in look forward to is a preposition; follow it with meeting.
We discussed about the budget.
We discussed the budget.
Discuss takes its topic directly; remove about.
He suggested me to rest.
He suggested that I rest.
Use suggested that followed by a clause here.
If I will see her, I will ask.
If I see her, I will ask.
For this future condition, use the present form in the if-clause.
The information are helpful.
The information is helpful.
Information is uncountable and takes is.
She bought two furnitures.
She bought two pieces of furniture.
Furniture is uncountable; count pieces of furniture.
I am used to wake early.
I am used to waking early.
Be used to means be accustomed to; follow it with an -ing form.
Neither of these keys work.
Conversational usage allows variation here. Works is a common formal choice; do not call this a definite error without context.
Could you send me the file?
This is a grammatical, polite request.
Who did you speak to?
This is natural English; ending with to is acceptable.
It's me.
This is standard conversational English.
Less sugar, please.
This is an appropriate conversational request.
The team are discussing their options.
Plural agreement with a collective noun is acceptable in British English.
I wish I were taller.
Were is appropriate for this hypothetical wish.
If I had known, I would have called.
This correctly describes an unreal past condition.
I have already eaten.
This is a grammatical present-perfect sentence.
